episode_title: The Confidence Economy Why Trust Is the Most Valuable Thing You Can Build
question: How does Simplified SEO Consulting build trust with employees through decision-making transparency?
transcript_excerpt: Mary and Winnie explain that they communicate the why behind decisions clearly to their team rather than just giving directives. When decisions affect the team, they go back to employees and explain both the decision and the reasoning. They also maintain open communication channels where team members feel safe discussing concerns without fear of retaliation, and they address accountability issues collaboratively rather than defensively.

episode_title: The Confidence Economy Why Trust Is the Most Valuable Thing You Can Build
question: What role do referrals and professional recommendations play in the confidence economy?
transcript_excerpt: Winnie states that referrals are not just about sending clients but about someone lending part of the trust they have built with their own audience. When someone refers a client, they are trusting the referred business to take good care of that person. Simplified SEO Consulting practices this by reciprocating—for example, when Google Ads might be a better fit than SEO, they refer clients to John at Revkey, whom they trust to work well with mental health providers.

episode_title: The Confidence Economy Why Trust Is the Most Valuable Thing You Can Build
question: How can business owners reduce work stress from affecting family relationships and trust?
transcript_excerpt: Mary emphasizes creating a work environment that is as stress-free, calm, and trusting as possible so employees don't take work stress home. She highlights that Simplified SEO Consulting fosters contentment through open communication, humor in team chat, and creating an environment where people look forward to coming to work. When stress does occur, being upfront with family about difficult weeks and creating boundaries—such as not requiring team members to have email on their phones during time off—helps preserve family trust.

episode_title: The Confidence Economy Why Trust Is the Most Valuable Thing You Can Build
question: What does trusting yourself mean when you struggle with perfectionism and imposter syndrome?
transcript_excerpt: Winnie explains that trusting yourself is not the same as believing you always make perfect choices. She describes struggling as a perfectionist who sets impossible standards, but realizes that trusting yourself means accepting that it's okay to make mistakes, to change course when new information appears, and to take responsibility without viewing yourself as a failure. The key is making small promises to yourself and keeping them—not sacrificing your own needs repeatedly to help others.

episode_title: The Confidence Economy Why Trust Is the Most Valuable Thing You Can Build
question: How does allowing others to see your vulnerabilities strengthen self-trust and support?
transcript_excerpt: Mary shares a personal story about bowling with a mobility device and initially doubting she belonged there. When she voiced her internal struggle to her friend, the friend was able to support her by capturing her achievement and publicly celebrating it. Mary concludes that trusting yourself doesn't mean doing everything alone—sometimes it means allowing people who have built trust with you to help you see yourself more accurately and support you through difficult moments.
